lines.text: When I was ten, Dad bought my brother and me two old walkie-talkies at a yard sale.
Inside one battery door was a note, in a kid's handwriting.
Never use channel nine after dark. And if anyone asks where you are... don't tell them.
Every night, Danny and I talked from our beds, across the hall. Always on channel two.
Then, one night, in a thunderstorm, the static changed.
My dial clicked to nine... all by itself.
A small voice whispered, Is anyone there? I'm lost.
I didn't answer. I just listened to it breathe.
Then Danny cut in, on channel nine. I'm scared. Where are you?
I pressed the button. My room, I whispered. Come here.
I ran across the hall. Danny was fast asleep. His walkie-talkie sat on the dresser... with no batteries.
Behind me, my radio crackled. Thank you, it said, in Danny's voice. Now I know which room.
We moved away that week. Nothing came for twenty years.
Last night, my daughter found them in the attic. She asked who the little boy on channel nine is... and why he keeps asking which room is mine now.
